source_text: Ὡς δὲ καὶ λήσειν ἔμελλε τοὺς ἄλλους ἀνθρώπους γεννηθεὶς ὁ Χριστὸς ἄχρις ἀνδρωθῇ. ὅπερ καὶ γέγονεν, ἀκούσατε τῶν προειρημένων εἰς τοῦτο. Ἔστι δὲ ταῦτα· „Παιδίον ἐγεννήθη ἡμῖν, καὶ νεανίσκος ἡμῖν ἀπεδόθη, οὗ ἡ ἀρχ(??) ἐπὶ τῶν ὤμων“· μηνυτικὸν τῆς δυνάμεως τοῦ σταυροῦ, ᾧ προσέθηκε τοὺς ὤμους σταυρωθείς, ὡς πρωϊόντος τοῦ λόγον σαφέστερον δειχθήσεται. Καὶ πάλιν ὁ αὐτὸς προφήτης Ἡσαΐας θεοφορούμενος τῷ πνεύματι τῷ προφητικῷ ἔφη· ,Ἐγώ ἐξεπέτασα τὰς χεῖράς μου ἐπὶ λαὸν ἀπειθοῦντα καὶ ἀντιλέγοντα, ἐπὶ τοὺς πορευομένους ἐν ὁδῷ οὐ καλῇ. Αἰτοῦσί με νῦν κρίσιν καὶ ἐγγίζειν θεῷ τολμῶσιν“. Καὶ πάλιν ἐν ἄλλοις λόγοις δι᾿ ἑτέρου προφήτου λέγει· „Αὐιοὶ ὤρυξάν μου πόδας καὶ χεῖρας, καὶ ἔβαλον κλῆρον ἐπὶ τὸν ἱματισμόν μου“. Καὶ ὁ μὲν Δαυῒδ ὁ βασιλεὺς καὶ προφήτης, ὁ εἰπὼν ταῦτα, οὐδὲν τούτων ἔπαθεν· Ἰησοῦς δὲ Χριστὸς ἐξετάθη τὰς χεῖρας, σταυρωθεὶς ὑπὸ τῶν Ἰουδαίων ἀντιλεγόντων αὐτῷ καὶ φασκόντων μὴ εἶναι αὐτὸν Χριστόν· καὶ γάρ, ὡς εἶπεν ὁ προφήτης, διασύροντες αὐτὸν ἐκάθισαν ἐπὶ βήματος καὶ εἶπον· Κρῖνον ἡμῖν. Τὸ δὲ „Ὤρυξάν μου χεῖρας καὶ πόδας‘· ἐξήγησις τῶν ἐν τῷ σταυρῷ παγέντων ἐν ταῖς χερσὶ καὶ τοῖς ποσὶν αὐτοῦ ἥλων ἦν. Καὶ μετὰ τὸ σταυρῶσαι αὐτὸν ἔβαλον κλῆρον ἐπὶ τὸν ἱματισμὸν αὐτοῦ καὶ ἐμερίσαντο ἑαυτοῖς οἱ σταυρώσαντες αὐτόν. Καὶ ταῦτα ὅτι γέγονε, δύνασθε μαθεῖν ἐκ τῶν ἐπὶ Ποντίου Πιλάτου γενομένων ἄκτων. Καὶ ὅτι ῥητῶς καθεσθησόμενος ἐπὶ πῶλον ὄνου καὶ εἰσελευσόμενος εἰς τὰ Ἱεροσόλυμα προεπεφήτευτο, ἑτέρου προφήτου τοῦ Σοφονίου τας τῆς προφητείας λέξεις ἐροῦμεν. Εἰσὶ δὲ αὗται· „Χαῖρε σφόδρα, θύγατερ Σιών, κήρυσσε, θύγατερ Ἱερουσαλήμ· ἰδοὺ ὁ βασιλεύς σου ἔρχεται σοι πρᾶος, ἐπιβεβηκὼς ἐπὶ ὄνον καὶ πῶλον υἱὸν ὑποζυγίου“.
pass_a_gloss: As also He was about to release the other humans, having been born, Christ, until He becomes a man. Which also happened, hear from the previously mentioned things to this effect. There are these things: A child was born to us, and a young man was given to us, whose authority is upon His shoulders; a sign of the power of the cross, to which He drew near His shoulders having been crucified, as will be shown more clearly in the morning of the word. And again the same prophet Isaiah, being borne by the prophetic Spirit, said: I stretched out my hands to a disobedient people and those speaking against, to those walking in a way not good. They ask me now for judgment and dare to draw near to God. And again in other words through another prophet He says: They dug my hands and feet, and they cast lots for my clothing. And David the king and prophet, who said these things, did not suffer any of these things; but Jesus Christ was examined as to His hands, having been crucified by the Jews who spoke against Him and said He was not the Christ; and indeed, as the prophet said, dragging Him, they sat on the judgment seat and said: Judge us. The They dug my hands and feet is an explanation of the things happening on the cross, the nails in His hands and feet. And after they crucified Him, they cast lots for His clothing and divided it among themselves, those who crucified Him. And that these things happened, you are able to learn from the acts that took place under Pontius Pilate. And that having been explicitly set upon a foal of a donkey and entering into Jerusalem was prophesied, we will speak the words of the prophecy of another prophet, Zechariah. These are: Rejoice greatly, daughter of Zion, proclaim, daughter of Jerusalem: behold your king comes to you, gentle, mounted upon a donkey and a foal, a son of a beast of burden.

choices.why: indicating the action of the prophet
indicating the clarity of the prophecy

pass_b_english: Christ was born in order to release the other human beings, and He did so after He became a man, as the earlier prophecies declare (Isaiah 9:6). For it says: "A child was born to us, and a young man was given to us, whose authority rests upon His shoulders," which is a sign of the power of the cross; He laid hold of His shoulders by being crucified, and this will be shown more clearly as the Word advances.

Again the same prophet Isaiah, carried by the prophetic Spirit, said: "I stretched out My hands all day long to a disobedient and contrary people, to those who walk in a way that is not good. They ask Me now for judgment and dare to draw near to God" (Isaiah 65:2; 58:2).

And again He says through another prophet: "They pierced my hands and my feet, and they cast lots for my clothing" (Psalm 22:16-18). King and prophet David, who spoke these words, did not suffer any of these things; but Jesus Christ was examined regarding His hands when He was crucified by the Jews who opposed Him and claimed He was not the Christ.

Indeed, as the prophet said, they dragged Him, sat on the judgment seat, and said: "Judge for us." The words "They pierced my hands and feet" explain the nails driven through His hands and feet on the cross. After they crucified Him, they cast lots for His clothing and divided it among themselves, the very ones who crucified Him. You can verify that these things happened from the official records compiled under Pontius Pilate.

And because it was explicitly prophesied that He would sit upon a donkey's colt and enter Jerusalem, we will cite the words of the prophecy from another prophet, Zechariah (Zechariah 9:9): "Rejoice greatly, daughter of Zion; shout aloud, daughter of Jerusalem: behold, your king comes to you, gentle and mounted on a donkey, on a colt, the foal of a beast of burden."

review.notes: Pass B adds specific scripture citations (Isaiah 9:6, Isaiah 65:2; 58:2, Psalm 22:16-18, Zechariah 9:9) that are not present in the Locked Greek text. While these are historically accurate to the verses being quoted, the instructions state: 'A summary is not a translation' and 'Pass B must neither add to nor contradict A or the Greek.' Pass B introduces external data (verse numbers) not found in the source. Additionally, Pass A contains a significant mistranslation of the final clause: 'υἱὸν ὑποζυγίου' is translated as 'a son of a beast of burden', whereas in context (and in Pass B) it refers to the 'foal of a beast of burden' (the colt), which is the standard translation for the Greek idiom here; 'son of a beast of burden' is a literalist error that obscures the meaning.
reasons: Pass B adds scripture citations (e.g., 'Isaiah 9:6', 'Psalm 22:16-18') not present in the Locked Greek source.
Pass A mistranslates 'υἱὸν ὑποζυγίου' as 'a son of a beast of burden' instead of 'a foal of a beast of burden' (or 'colt'), which changes the sense of the noun phrase.
